title: The Fake 'Original Price' Is Stealing $2,600 From You
hook: That 'was $199, now $97' tag? In most stores, the $199 was never real. Reference price fraud costs the average shopper $2,600 a year — and it's completely legal.
angle: Reference price deception — stores set artificial 'original' prices almost never actually charged, then 'discount' to them to manipulate perceived value. The FTC has documented this extensively and Amazon settled a class action over it in 2022.
audience: Online shoppers, bargain hunters, anyone who makes purchase decisions based on sale prices or 'was/now' tags
key_numbers: 85% of reference prices were never actually charged (FTC investigation)
$2,600 average annual overspend from reference price manipulation
Amazon settled class action over fake reference prices in 2022
Fake anchor raises perceived value by 40%
